There may be a limited decline in dependency on public assistance during construction of the conversion plant but this dependency may increase sharply if operational or other economic activities do not absorb the released construction labor force.
During the brief construction period requirements for educational facilities and personnel probably would increase far beyond the capacity of the area to expand. The present acute housing situation in the area would become even more acute and the sudden influx of people may result in the creation of slum areas which may be hard to eliminate after the construction period is over.
Health services and law and order capabilities would be initially badly overloaded and would require very significant expansion to accomodate the increased population even after the construction period is over. Similar impacts on municipal water, sewer and waste disposal facilities would be expected and serious financing problems would be anticipated.
The sudden increase in population and the resultant forced crowding of people of different backgrounds may result in serious changes in social behavior, including serious strained relations between different social groups resulting in social discord. Social instability, associated with rapidly urbanizing areas and the weakening of traditional social structures including families, may be expected to result in a higher incidence of serious deviancy, including criminal action, dependency on drugs (particularly on alcohol), as well as a disregard for property and civil rights.
